$comment: Every third-party dependency and every ML model, with its licence.
tools/check_licences.py validates this file in CI and fails the build on
anything that breaks the ADR 0006 policy: free in perpetuity, closed-source
Adding a dependency means adding it here first. The gate also cross-checks
that anything CMake fetches or vcpkg installs is declared.
'cmakeNames' lists the names a dependency is found under in build files, because a package is rarely called the same thing twice.

'systemPackages' exempts a find_package() that is a platform facility rather than a third-party library -- the compiler's threading runtime, the system's own OpenGL. Each needs a reason, so every exemption is written down rather than assumed.

dependencies.name: alsa-lib
dependencies.usedFor: Audio output on Linux, behind sa::device::AudioDevice.
dependencies.notes: LGPL-2.1, so linked dynamically against the system libasound; the user can replace it. Optional: src/sa-device/CMakeLists.txt guards it with find_package(ALSA) and the module builds without it, exactly as the UI does with Qt. Not shipped -- it is the distribution's own library. Windows uses WASAPI from the platform SDK, which needs no entry here.

dependencies.name: nlohmann_json
dependencies.purpose: Session file parsing. Session files are untrusted input -- a user opens one someone sent them -- so this uses a well-tested parser rather than a hand-rolled one, the same reasoning that made us write our own WAV parser go the other way: there we needed metadata control the libraries do not offer; here we need robustness we would have to earn from scratch.

dependencies.name: qtbase
dependencies.purpose: Application shell and widgets. LGPL-3.0, so DYNAMIC LINKING ONLY -- see docs/05-licensing-and-dependencies.md section 5 for the relink and source-offer obligations that come with it. Qt Charts, Qt Data Visualization and Qt Virtual Keyboard are GPL-only and must never be linked.
